title: Winspace M6 Review: It's Fast, but...

takeaways.text: Frame supplied by Winspace. Size L frame 1,000 g (about 90 g lighter than his T1600), fork 450 g, seatpost 175 g, Hyper cockpit 335 g; the complete build with pedals, cages and mount weighed 7.8 kg.

Routing the front brake hose to the fork exit was slow; headset bearings differ in size so cannot be swapped, brake mounts were flat, UDH is fitted but there is no internal Di2 battery holder, and no manual is included.
An endoscope showed clean main tubes, a visible seam where front and rear sections join near the chainstays, and a small epoxy remnant in the fork, judged not structural.
Stiff and fast once up to speed, but with more road vibration than the T1600 on identical wheels and tires, and the deep fork needs more attention in gusty crosswinds for a 70 kg rider.

About US$1,880 for the frameset plus US$400 for the cockpit (August 2026); an Ultegra Di2 complete was about US$4,900. Direct delivery can take up to three months in busy periods; import fees are handled by Winspace.

disclosure: The description discloses affiliate commissions and a Winspace discount code. Product-supply terms are not established there.
summary: M6 review of an Ultegra Di2 and UPVINE Pro+ custom build. It complements the existing shop-tour context without resolving the candidate's mainland China coupon-card configuration.
